approval_required_for: Any architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, runtime-layout, numeric-policy, or major template change proposed from Stage7 replay results.
Any attempt to change golden outputs, tolerances, selected checkers, or verification hierarchy instead of rerunning the clean contract; this role does not authorize waivers.
Any board/runtime/Vivado/AXI/DDR wrapped-system execution before clean operator-leaf and clean single-transformer-layer promotion certificates exist.
Any modification to the promoted Stage6 gate selector, failure-localization schema, or debug-trace schema outside the Stage6 ownership boundary.
Any backend/app-shell target-discovery or target-name selection if later board evidence is ambiguous; it must be handled by the backend board-integration authority, not this replay planner.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not run Stage7 replay. Keep current Stage7 artifacts debug-only and hand back to Stage6 verification-artifact repair or SACG trust-barrier reconciliation with the failed checker list.
executable_actions.rationale: Before any Stage7 rerun, the replay planner must prove that the consumed Stage6 verification artifacts are promoted, complete, and bound to the case adapter/tool protocols. This prevents reuse of rejected Stage6 contracts and makes the rerun scope checker-grounded.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not consume prior Stage7 operator-leaf evidence in the clean rerun. Require Stage7 verification to start from the promoted Stage6 contract without debug-seed promotion, or return to Stage6 if the replay scope cannot be derived.
executable_actions.rationale: Prior operator-leaf results and promotion certificates were produced under rejected transitions. They may guide localization but must be explicitly quarantined and rebound to a clean replay scope before any checker can consume them.

executable_actions.on_failure: Stop at operator-leaf layer. Send the failed real-tool logs and debug traces to failure localization; do not issue an operator-leaf promotion certificate and do not start single-layer or backend work.
executable_actions.rationale: The first hardware-debug layer must be rerun under the clean Stage6 contract. Fresh operator-leaf evidence must cover boundary contract, static case checks, functional execution, golden/numeric compare, data order, transfer count, artifact hashes, and liveness/deadlock behavior for the selected scope.

executable_actions.on_failure: Stop at the connected single-transformer-layer layer. Preserve operator-leaf pass evidence, localize the single-layer failing boundary/transaction, and route only the causal slice to Stage8 bounded repair. Do not start AXI/DDR, Vivado, runtime, or board checks.
executable_actions.rationale: Only after a fresh operator-leaf pass may the connected single-transformer-layer kernel be checked. This gate verifies cross-operator integration, stream order, beat/transfer alignment, numeric policy, and liveness before any board-accurate wrapping is considered.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not propose RTL/template/code repair from unlocalized failure evidence. Backtrack to Stage6 if schemas or gate contracts are incomplete; otherwise rerun the failed checker with additional trace capture under the same clean contract.
executable_actions.rationale: A failed replay layer must enter the contract-guided debug loop before repair: tool output, boundary/transaction localization, causal context packing, and bounded Stage8 handoff. This prevents broad or premature code changes.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep downstream backend/board artifacts blocked, open or maintain the Stage7 retry request, and route failure evidence through localization before any repair or higher-layer verification.
executable_actions.rationale: The replay result must drive the next tool decision. Backend, board, AXI/DDR, Vivado, runtime ABI, bitstream, and board-runtime stages remain blocked unless both clean operator-leaf and clean single-layer gates pass with required real-tool evidence.

observations: The supplied state summary records active contamination barriers on Stage6 verification artifacts, Stage7 verification outputs, Stage7 debug closure, Stage7 operator-leaf promotion certificates, and Stage8 repair artifacts, plus open retry requests targeting Stage6 and Stage7. This plan is therefore conditional: Stage7 rerun is executable only after clean Stage6 artifacts are promoted and the relevant trust barriers/retry state are reconciled by the owning gates.

No open backtrack request is listed in the supplied SACG truth summary; the current bounded path is retry after clean Stage6 promotion, not architecture backtrack, unless the Stage7 preflight finds the repaired Stage6 contract still incomplete.

Existing Stage7 operator-leaf evidence may have passed within a rejected scope, but it is not validated promotion evidence. It can only be consumed as debug-only localization context until operator-leaf gates are rerun under the clean Stage6 verification contract.

The candidate artifact shows contract-guided debug-closure and hierarchical repair-loop diagnostics are present, while case_vcs_functional is null. A null or not_run real-tool field is an evidence gap, not hardware correctness.

The required hierarchy is operator/leaf first, then connected single-transformer-layer kernel. Board-accurate AXI/DDR wrapping, Vivado, runtime ABI, and board execution remain blocked and out of this role’s execution scope until the lower hierarchy gates pass with real-tool evidence.

Data order, transfer count/beat alignment, numeric comparison, and liveness/deadlock checks must be attached to the selected operator-leaf and single-layer replay scopes rather than inferred from prior rejected artifacts.
proposed_actions: After clean Stage6 promotion, run a Stage7 preflight trust gate over the promoted verification plan, artifact contract, LLM audit, gate selector, debug trace schema, failure localization schema, tool protocols, and SACG references.
Record all previous Stage7 operator-leaf debug closure and promotion-certificate artifacts as debug-only replay seeds; do not promote or use them as pass evidence.
Generate a clean failure_localization_replay_scope and operator_leaf_then_single_layer_gate_sequence from the promoted Stage6 gate selector.

Rerun operator-leaf static, functional, golden/numeric compare, data-order, transfer-count, and liveness/deadlock checks under the clean contract; only a fresh pass can produce a clean operator-leaf promotion certificate.

If operator-leaf passes, rerun the connected single-transformer-layer functional, golden/numeric compare, data-order, transfer-count, and liveness/deadlock checks; do not skip directly to board or backend execution.

On any failed Stage7 layer, localize the earliest failing boundary/transaction using debug traces and the failure-localization schema, pack causal repair context, and hand off to Stage8 bounded repair without promoting the failed layer.
Keep backend/board/Vivado/runtime artifacts blocked until the hierarchy gate status proves clean operator-leaf and clean single-layer passes with required real-tool evidence.
risks: Contamination risk: promoting artifact.stage7.operator_leaf_promotion_certificate or artifact.stage7.debug_closure from a rejected transition would bypass SACG trust barriers and create a false Stage7 pass.

Contract risk: if the promoted Stage6 artifacts do not include a complete stage7_gate_selector_contract, failure_localization_schema, and debug_trace_manifest_schema, Stage7 cannot produce bounded replay evidence and must return to Stage6 contract repair.

Real-tool evidence risk: case_vcs_functional is null in the candidate artifact, so functional, liveness, and numeric correctness cannot be claimed until the selected real tools produce fresh results under the clean contract.

Cross-layer consistency risk: stream order, beat/transfer count, memory/runtime address assumptions, and numeric policy may diverge between operator-leaf and connected single-layer scopes if the rerun does not bind the same clean Stage6 contract and case adapter.

Premature backend risk: starting AXI/DDR, Vivado, runtime ABI, bitstream, or board-runtime work before operator-leaf and single-layer hierarchy gates pass would violate the verification hierarchy and could hide the earliest causal failure boundary.

Localization risk: if a replay fails, repairing code before boundary-localized tool evidence is packed would violate the required tool-output to CCTG/contract-guided localization to bounded repair loop.
output.summary: Stage7 must be rerun from the operator/leaf boundary after clean Stage6 verification artifacts are promoted and SACG trust barriers are reconciled. Existing Stage7 operator-leaf evidence and promotion certificates from rejected transitions remain debug-only seeds; they cannot be promoted until rerun under the clean Stage6 contract. The bounded sequence is: clean Stage6 trust gate, quarantine/rebind old leaf evidence, rerun operator-leaf real-tool gates, then rerun connected single-transformer-layer gates, with failure localization and Stage8 handoff on any failed layer and no backend/board/Vivado/runtime progression before hierarchy gates pass.
